historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Management guidance (mid-single-digit organic, ~2x global IP) cross-checked against the 5-yr revenue and equity CAGRs of 7.4%, which are inflated by the FY2020 COVID-trough base and the FY2022 Vulcanic/Durex acquisitions; the 3-yr CAGRs (1.9% revenue, 1.5% equity) are depressed by a ~3%/yr sterling headwind and the FY2025 restructuring charge. Organic growth FY2023-H1 2026 ran 4-6%.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR 7.4% diverges >30% from EPS 5-yr CAGR of -1.2% (statutory EPS depressed by the FY2025 GBP39.9m restructuring charge, acquired-intangible amortisation and FX); adjusted EPS grew 296.3p FY2025 vs 273.8p FY2020-ish base, i.e. low single digits. Growth is set from guidance, not from the equity CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC; interest sits outside OCF): 2019 158.8, 2020 202.6, 2021 200.1, 2022 114.7, 2023 187.1, 2024 216.9, 2025 221.8. The 3-yr figure is off the FY2022 trough (117.5m capex year, Vulcanic/Durex integration) and is not a trend. SBC is a trivial 0.2-0.7% of revenue, so owner and reported CAGRs are within 0.1pt of each other -- SBC is not where the growth is being paid for. Lease-consistent owner FCF (also less 21.2m lease cash) was 200.6m in FY2025.

scenario_narratives.base: Guidance delivered and sustained: mid-single-digit organic growth at ~2x IP fading to GDP-like by year 10, half the CMD margin ambition achieved (adjusted operating margin ~21.3% by FY2032), capex normalising at 4.5% and cash tax at 25%. Terminal value at 2.5% growth, Gordon-bound below the 18x cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: CMD medium-term targets fully delivered and exceeded: ETS to 20% margin on Semicon/Datacentre/Heat Trace, WMFTS Biopharm recovery to 30%+ margin, STS large-project recovery plus decarbonisation TAM. ~6% organic growth for five years, adjusted operating margin ~23%, terminal growth 3%, 20x cap.
scenario_narratives.bear: Weak-IP, strong-sterling, WMFTS-competition case: growth 1-2.5%, adjusted operating margin erodes to ~18.8%, capex and working-capital intensity stay elevated, terminal 2% and a 15x cap. A derating, not a distress case.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Spirax is valued as a going-concern owner-FCF stream in GBP, with SBC expensed and the count held flat, leases charged in the flows (treatment B) and excluded from net debt, acquired-intangible amortisation ignored as non-cash, and cash tax ramped to a normal 25% from a flattered FY2025 rate. The 8.5% GBP WACC is held constant across scenarios; business risk is priced in the scenario paths and a 25/50/25 weighting. The market has historically paid 25-35x adjusted earnings for this franchise; the house model does not assume that premium persists in the terminal (Gordon at 2.5% binds below the 18x FCF cap), so a gap between house IV and price is the price of the quality premium, stated rather than assumed.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin path: each 1pt of pre-IFRS-16 EBITDA margin is ~GBP17-20m of EBITDA, roughly 5-6% of base-case value; the CMD divisional targets (which imply ~23% group adjusted margin) are only half-captured in base.
Global IP below 2% for a fourth year and continued sterling strength keep reported growth 2-3pt below organic; the model's growth rates are reported-currency.
Watson-Marlow competitive position: a scaled entrant (Ingersoll Rand) in peristaltic/bioprocessing fluid paths threatens the Group's highest-margin division (27.5% H1 2026).
Working-capital intensity (25.7% of sales) means growth consumes cash; the -20% capture assumption is calibrated to FY2025 and could be worse in strong ETS growth years (H1 2026 conversion 54%).
Net debt is taken at the seasonal June high (618.2) rather than the expected ~1.5x year-end level; this understates value by roughly 50-70p/share.
Bolt-on M&A (~GBP10m/yr historically, larger in 2022) is not modelled; it is both a use of cash and a source of growth not captured in organic paths.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (regularMarketPrice, GBp) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 5950-8050p.
data_sources.financials: SPX.L_Metrics.csv / core_metrics FY2019-FY2025 and H1 2025, H1 2026 (GBP millions); FY2025 Annual Report cash flow statement, adjusted cash flow and net debt reconciliation (p.~171 and CFO review), Note 23 net debt, EBITDA definition note; H1 2026 interim Notes 5 (diluted shares) and 8 (net debt, lease liabilities, borrowings), adjusted cash flow table.
data_sources.qualitative: SPX.L_Analysis.json (2026-10-10): business model, CMD medium-term targets, H1 2026 guidance, bull/bear axes; FY2025 Annual Report outlook and 2026 guidance section.

inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted average 73.9m (H1 2026 interim, Note 5; identical to basic -- dilution immaterial). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would double-charge it. No non-SBC issuance expected.
inputs.net_debt_note: Company definition at 30 June 2026 (H1 2026 Note 8): borrowings 783.5 + overdrafts 213.0 = 996.5 gross debt, less cash and equivalents 378.3 = 618.2 (1.6x EBITDA). Lease liabilities of 89.3 are EXCLUDED because leases are charged inside the flows (treatment B). June is the seasonal high point (final dividend and H1 working-capital build); FY2025 year-end net debt was 564.7. The latest filing is used regardless.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report cash flow statement, 'Equity settled share plans' add-back GBP6.4m (FY2024 3.1, FY2023 6.1); no separate equity-award tax line (EquityAwardTaxes 0 across history). H1 2026 add-back was 5.4m, so the forward path is set at 0.5% of revenue rather than the FY2025 0.38%.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest received (FY2025 GBP8.7m) sits in INVESTING activities in Spirax's cash flow statement and interest paid in FINANCING, so reported OCF/FCF of 228.2 is already pre-interest (unlevered). Nothing to strip; and the company is a net debtor (net debt 618.2), so the net-cash double-count rule does not apply.
inputs.buyback_note: No repurchases FY2024-H1 2026. FY2019-FY2023 'ShareRepurchases' of 12.8-26.1m were purchases of own shares for employee share plans, not a capital-return programme. The flat count is a modelling convention the company funds through employee-plan share purchases, not a buyback.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp). 1 GBP = 100 GBp by definition, not a market rate, so no date/source/parity check applies. All per-share outputs are computed in GBP and multiplied by 100 to the pence quote basis.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T15:41:51Z regular close (LSE), Yahoo Finance chart API; 52-week range 5950-8050p
inputs.wacc_rationale: GBP-built: 10y gilt ~4.5%, ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.9 (FTSE 100 defensive industrial, 85% of sales MRO/solution-sales from opex budgets) -> cost of equity ~9.0%; after-tax cost of debt ~3.5% (USPP/term loans, 27% tax); market-value weights ~90/10 -> WACC 8.5%. The same WACC is used in all three scenarios; cyclicality, WMFTS competition and FX risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. Full lease cash (principal 18.0 + interest on lease liabilities 3.2 = 21.2m FY2025, 1.25% of revenue; H1 2026 9.1 + 1.6) is deducted inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (89.3m) are EXCLUDED from net debt. EBITDA margin is therefore stated PRE-IFRS-16 (adjusted operating profit + owned D&A + ROU depreciation + SBC), and da_pct is owned D&A only (PPE, software, development: 46.0m = 2.7% of revenue) so the lease is not charged twice in the tax line. Acquired-intangible amortisation (34.6m) is excluded from the build throughout (it is non-cash and has no replacement capex).
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interest profit share is 0.2m/yr (immaterial); flows treated as fully attributable, no NCI deduction in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical: industrials') with the adaptations file applied for GBP WACC, GBp quote, IFRS 16 leases and NCI. Spirax is a thermal-energy / fluid-technology engineer with ~85% recurring opex-funded revenue, so a going-concern FCF model is the right frame; no financial/REIT/LIC element. FY0 is FY2025 (revenue 1702.9); year 1 of the build is FY2026, three-quarters elapsed at the valuation date but discounted a full year (end-of-year convention, slightly conservative). EBITDA ANCHOR: FY2025 adjusted operating profit 339.9 + owned D&A 46.0 + ROU depreciation 18.7 + SBC 6.4 = 411.0 = 24.1% of revenue, less ~0.4pt for ongoing defined-benefit pension contributions (7.1m cash, not in adjusted operating profit) = 23.7% effective FY2025 base; the FY2026 base-case 23.8% carries management's 'organic margin progress above the 2025 20.0%' guidance net of the ~2-3% FX headwind on reported figures. Component rebuild of FY2025 (EBIT 337.4, cash tax 65.9, capex 68.0, WC -18.6) gives 230.9 before the 22.1m restructuring cash and 7.1m pension cash that sit inside reported OCF, i.e. ties to the lease-consistent owner FCF of 200.6 (228.2 - 6.4 SBC - 21.2 lease); the restructuring programme completed in FY2025 (4.8m tail in H1 2026) and is not carried forward. CASH TAX: FY2025 taxes paid 65.9 = 19.5% of adjusted EBIT (FY2024 23%, FY2023 ~28%) against a 27.3% adjusted ETR; the path ramps 22% -> 25% because the FY2025 cash rate was flattered by deductible restructuring and acquired-intangible amortisation. WORKING CAPITAL: manufacturer with WC/sales 25.7% (H1 2026), so growth consumes cash: wc_capture_pct -20 on the revenue change. CAPEX: FY2026 guided ~4% of sales (FY2025 4.0%, FY2024 5.6%, FY2023 6.3% during the Ogden MV build); base ramps 4.0% -> 4.5%, the 5-year average ex the Ogden peak. GUIDANCE (H1 2026, reiterated): mid-single-digit organic revenue growth, organic margin above 20.0%, net financing / tax / cash conversion similar to 2025.

bear.narrative: FY2026 H2 undershoots (Middle East supply disruption, ETS against a +12% comparative), then global IP stays below 2% through 2028 with the five core markets (~50% of revenue) flat: STS large projects in China/Korea do not return, sterling strength keeps reported growth 2-3pt below organic, and Ingersoll Rand's integrated pump/tubing push takes share and price from Watson-Marlow so WMFTS margin slips below 27%. ETS stalls at 17-18% as Ogden ramp costs persist and 'pricing for value' is never implemented. Adjusted operating margin drifts to ~18.8% and stays there; working capital keeps absorbing 22% of each pound of growth and the restructuring savings are fully reinvested without return. No balance-sheet stress -- leverage stays inside covenants (3.5x) -- so this is a margin-and-multiple derating, not a solvency case.

base.narrative: FY2026 lands on guidance (mid-single-digit organic, ~4.5% reported after a small FX headwind), then organic growth at ~2x a 2% IP world fades to 2.5% by year 10. Pre-IFRS-16 EBITDA margin climbs 1.2pt over seven years (adjusted operating margin 20.0% -> ~21.3%), capturing roughly half the gap to the CMD divisional targets (STS 23.5 / ETS 20 / WMFTS 30 implies ~23% group) as ETS matures and WMFTS operating leverage returns. Capex ramps from the guided 4% to a 4.5% sustaining level; cash tax normalises to 25%.

bull.narrative: The Together for Growth targets are delivered in full and exceeded 'in the longer term' as management claims: ETS compounds at high-single/low-double digits on Semicon, Datacentre liquid-cooling and Heat Trace demand and reaches its 20% margin; WMFTS Biopharm orders (Q2 2026 highest since 2021) convert into high-single-digit growth at 30%+ margin; STS China/Korea large projects recover and decarbonisation (PoweringZero/TargetZero, ~GBP7bn added TAM) lifts STS above low-single-digit. Group adjusted operating margin reaches ~23% by year 8. Still organic only; bolt-on M&A is not modelled.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bull cut to 25% because it needs three independent things to go right at once (ETS margin delivery incl. Ogden ramp, WMFTS Biopharm conversion against a newly capitalised competitor, and an STS China/Korea project recovery) in a world where management itself plans on IP below consensus. Bear raised to 25% because reported growth has already run below the mid-single-digit target for three years (3-yr revenue CAGR 1.9%) on FX and weak IP, and because H1 2026 cash conversion (54%) showed how quickly working capital absorbs growth; it is capped there because 85% of revenue is opex-funded MRO/solution-sales with no customer >1% and the balance sheet carries no refinancing risk.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.sanity_check_note: scripts/sanity_check.py applies inputs.fx_rate backwards for GBP/GBp tickers (see memory sanity-check-fx-rate-direction-systemic-bug.md), inflating the printed implied_multiples and historical_table by fx_rate^2 (10,000x here). Hand-bridged (price_pence/100 x shares_millions = market_cap_GBP_millions) at the 7,270p current price and the 4,891.48p weighted IV: current price implies P/E 34.2x, P/B 4.4x, EV/EBITDA 16.4x, P/S 3.2x; the weighted IV implies P/E 23.0x, P/B 3.0x, EV/EBITDA 11.6x, P/S 2.1x. The 10yr hand-bridged historical range is P/B 4.1-11.7x and EV/EBITDA 14.0-31.5x (SBC-adjusted) -- both the current price and the DCF IV sit inside it. passed:true stands on this manual check, not on the printed (wrong-direction) numbers above.
